episode_title: Growth Now Movement Host on the 5 People Who Can Change Your Life

real_qa.q: What are the five specific roles Justin Schenck recommends for building an intentional support system in your life?
real_qa.r: Justin identifies five core roles: the cheerleader (like Chuck Balsamo) who lifts you up and helps you feel unstoppable; the bruiser (Coach Cav) who challenges your boundaries and makes you uncomfortable to grow; the softie (his wife) who supports you in difficult moments and helps you recover; a mentor (Fabio Viviani) who embodies qualities you want to develop; and a coach (in business, relationships, wellness, or spirituality) in whom you should be financially invested. These five people have remained relatively stable for several years and have been instrumental to his success.
real_qa.requete: five people roles support system Schenck

real_qa.q: How did Justin Schenck initially misunderstand Jim Rohn's famous quote about the five people you spend the most time with?
real_qa.r: At 19 years old after reading Who Moved My Cheese, Justin heard Jim Rohn's quote that 'you're the average of the five people you spend the most time with' and initially thought he needed to get rid of all his loser friends and find five millionaires to hang out with exclusively. He quickly realized that was stupid because no millionaire would want to hang out with a degenerate 19-year-old. He later discovered the quote didn't mean five literal friends, but rather five specific people filling distinct roles that he had subconsciously surrounded himself with throughout his growth from age 19 to 31-33.
real_qa.requete: Jim Rohn five people quote misunderstanding Justin Schenck

real_qa.q: What is Justin Schenck's approach to networking and building relationships without appearing salesy or transactional?
real_qa.r: Justin emphasizes that his approach is to walk into every room asking 'who can I support in this room?' rather than thinking about what he can get. By making conversations about the other person and focusing on their story instead of trying to impress them, he removes stress and nervousness from interactions. He calls this 'connecting' rather than 'networking,' and it has been fundamental to meeting major names and staying connected long-term. He also practices four non-negotiables daily, including checking in on somebody every single day to make sure they're good with a simple text.
real_qa.requete: building relationships without networking Justin Schenck approach

real_qa.q: What red flag does Justin Schenck look for when evaluating whether someone belongs in his inner circle?
real_qa.r: Justin looks for how people show up energetically and their patterns of behavior. A major red flag is when successful people only spend time with others at their level or above and don't pour into each other. He also watches for inconsistency across life areas—for example, he mentions that Tony Robbins' son told a story painting Tony as a terrible father, which made Justin realize you cannot be truly successful in one area while failing in others. He prioritizes integrity and character, emphasizing that being rich means nothing if you're not a good human being.
real_qa.requete: red flags spotting wrong people circle Justin Schenck

real_qa.q: How did Chuck Balsamo's unexpected Twitter message transform Justin Schenck's podcast career?
real_qa.r: When Justin was 14 episodes into his Growth Now Movement podcast with virtually no listeners, he received a message from Chuck Balsamo (a Twitter user with many followers) saying 'Justin, I love what you're doing with the podcast. I've been listening. Keep going. The content's amazing.' Justin reached out, Balsamo came on as episode 20, returned four more times, spoke multiple times at his events, and even officiated his wedding. Justin credits Balsamo as his ultimate encourager and biggest cheerleader, representing a turning point where he realized that unexpected support from the right person at the right moment could create a lifelong relationship and have profound impact.

guest.bio_context: Justin Schenck is an entrepreneur and podcaster who launched the Growth Now Movement podcast 10 years ago, which led to incredible conversations with amazing people and helped build multiple businesses. He is also the creator of Growth Now Summit Live and founder of podbrand.io. At age 19, he worked in a direct sales job where his manager introduced him to self-development through the book Who Moved My Cheese, which set him on a path of intentional growth and relationship building that shaped his entire career.
